what_it_does: AI models do enormous amounts of multiplication, and one way to speed those up is to use smaller, cruder numbers — a technique called quantization (storing weights as, say, 4-bit integers instead of 16-bit floats). The problem is that a small fraction of values in AI models are unusually large 'outliers,' and squeezing them into 4-bit form causes big accuracy losses. BLOOM tackles this by splitting values: outliers keep 8-bit precision while normal values drop to 4 bits, choosing the right format per value. It then stores these two precisions interleaved at the bit level (bit-slicing), so that the sparse, mostly-zero high-precision bits can be skipped during computation rather than processed through costly conversion logic. The result is faster inference with less accuracy loss than prior outlier-handling schemes, according to the abstract.
